body:
## Game Overview
**Battle of Origins** — nuzlocke dice tournament at `drbango.com/boobattles/`
**Repo:** `~/DrBango/boobattles/` (multi-file layered architecture)
**Card images:** `~/DrBango/tierlist/cards/` (JPG, referenced via `const IMG = '../tierlist/cards/'`)
**Current version:** v0.3

## Architecture (v0.3 — refactored 2026-04-04)
**10-layer pipeline** inspired by autonomous agent architecture:
```
index.html     — HTML shell + script loader (301 lines)
styles.css     — All visual styles (2900+ lines)
config.js      — CONFIG: IMG, CARDBACK, ABILITY_THEMES, ITEMS, DRAW_WEIGHTS
connectors.js  — CONNECTORS: ALL_GHOSTS (49 spirits, 5 rarities)
knowledge.js   — KNOWLEDGE BASE: BOSS_NAMES/HP/DROPS, LOCATIONS, buildBosses()
state.js       — STATE: game state, co-op state, save/load, battle variables
intelligence.js— INTELLIGENCE: boss scripts (BOSS0-11), varyScript(), drawGhost()
reports.js     — REPORTS: narration lines, Hall of Fame, run history
execution.js   — EXECUTION: dice mechanics, abilities, damage calc (~1540 lines)
presence.js    — PRESENCE: UI rendering, animations, effects (~1370 lines)
orchestrator.js— ORCHESTRATOR: game flow, VS mode, co-op campaign (~2030 lines)
```
- All functions are globals loaded as separate `<script>` tags (not modules)
- Cross-layer references work at runtime since all are in global scope
- Also deployed at `drbango.com/arch/` as standalone reference

## Modes
1. **Campaign (Nuzlocke)** — 12-boss tournament, permadeath, team building
2. **VS Mode** — Local 2-player PvP, simultaneous rolling
3. **2v2 Co-op Campaign** (v0.3) — 2 players co-op through 12 bosses

## 2v2 Co-op Campaign (v0.3)
- Both players pick starters (P1 from 3, P2 from remaining 2)
- Each boss fight = boss + random partner ghost (scaled HP by fight number)
- Partner scaling: fights 0-3 commons +0-1HP, 4-7 uncommons/rares +1-2HP, 8-11 rares/ghost-rares +2-3HP
- Players alternate turns, choose which enemy to target
- Real boss scripts, real draw weights, real item drops
- Both players get rewards (item + draw 2 ghosts, pick 1 each)
- Permadeath per player's collection, shared campaign progress
- `coopState` saved to localStorage separately from campaign state
- **Known fix:** `doEnemyRoll()` uses `state.currentBoss` — must check `coopMode ? coopState.currentBoss` instead

## Balance Philosophy
- **First fight (Logey):** Always scripted, player dice max 4 (no 5s/6s), low doubles (1s, 2s). Guaranteed win tutorial.
- **Bosses 0-2:** Always scripted, guaranteed wins
- **Bosses 3-8:** 50/50 script vs random, 50%/round breakout
- **Bosses 9-11 (finals):** 50/50 script vs random, 20% breakout for epic arcs
- **King Jay:** Reflection-focused, NO triples. 45% reflect (total=7), 25% doubles, 30% random. Rage: 55%/30%/15%
- **Hector:** Singles beat doubles BOTH WAYS (universal rule in his fights)
- **1 HP clutch:** All ghosts get 20% doubles + 10% triples at 1 HP (campaign only). Underdog gets 40%/30%
- **Rage mode:** King Jay & Hector get boosted modifiers below 30% HP

## Ghost Hidden Dice Modifiers
- Wim (Slash): 15% force all-odd
- Guard Thomas (Stoic): 15% triples, 20% doubles
- Masked Hero (Underdog): 40% triples + 30% doubles at 1 HP; 3 dmg counter vs before-rolling effects
- Kairan (Let's Dance): 10% force doubles
- Dream Cat (Jinx): 15% force doubles (synergizes with Jinx passive)
- Tommy Salami (Regulator): enemies 40%/die → 5/6, rerolled to 1-3. +1 dmg per rerolled die on win
- Roger (Tempest): 80% force 2 pairs with 4+ dice
- Romy (enemy): 50% chance to "read" own dice for correct prediction
- General: 15% quad boost when rolling 4+ dice (excludes Tempest)

## Featured Draw Rates
- Balatron: 15%, Kairan: 15%, Eloise: 18%, Guard Thomas: 18%
- Romy: 12% (after boss 4), Katrina: 8% (after boss 4)
- Patrick: 50% filtered OUT of pool

## Not In Game (sideline-only abilities)
17 ghosts: Ancient One, Bandit Pete, Bilbo, Dallas, Gary, Gus, Jeanie, Laura, Lou, Mallow, Mr. Filbert, Nicholas, Night Master, Pale Nimbus, Sandwiches, Suspicious Jeff, Zach

## VS Mode
- Red action bar with activatable abilities + ice shard/sacred fire commitment
- Red Bogey uses manual arming (not auto-reflect)
- No 180° rotation — everything right-side-up, color-coded
- Winner screen themed by color ("Blue Wins!" / "Red Wins!")

## Custom Ability Splash Themes
- Seeker: deep blue with cyan flash + pulse
- Let's Dance: fiery orange burst with slam-rotate entrance
- Reflect (Bogey/King Jay): mirror shimmer sweep, white/ice-blue glass effect
- Heinous: dark red pulse
- Bogus shield: blue shield glow

## Key Fixes (v0.3.1 — 2026-04-07)
- Outlaw Thief now triggers on doubles win/loss/tie (was winner-only, broken vs Pelter)
- Pelter forced doubles capped at 1-5 (was rolling double-6s too often)
- Dream Cat 15% doubles boost added
- 15% quad boost for 4+ dice rolls (excludes Tempest)

## Key Fixes (v0.2)
- Doubles kicker tie-breaking, Patrick bypasses Stoic, Patrick advances script round
- King Jay checks defender's dice for Reflection, Antoinette Grace works player-side
- Enemy dice display up to 7 slots, Powder Final Gift all death paths
- Piper Slick Coat fully implemented, Flora heals on wins AND losses
- Map screen: Tournament Road with progress bar, location themes, dramatic boss entrance

## Easter Eggs
- 2% silly rolling narration ("*blows on dice*", "come on triples", etc.)

## Remaining TODO
1. Co-op polish — test all 12 bosses, verify reward flow, fix any remaining state.X crashes
2. Sound polish — ability SFX, Six City fanfare
3. Mobile testing — action bar cramping on small screens
4. Replay hooks — speed run timer? harder difficulty? different starters?
5. Sideline system — would unlock 17 more ghosts if implemented

## Battle of Origins — The Board Game
**URL:** drbango.com/boardgame/
**Repo:** ~/DrBango/boardgame/ (WyattinTexas/DrBango)
**Version:** v0.4 (2026-04-05)

### What it is
Board game adaptation of the Arch Nuzlocke mode. Travel a node-based map, find items, make event choices, battle monsters with dice combat. Same ghost roster (36 spirits), card art, and abilities as Arch.

### Architecture
- `index.html` — all screens (title, pick, map, event, prebattle, battle, reward, gameover, win)
- `data.js` — ghost database, items (combat + key items), events, regions, encounter weights
- `map.js` — node graph generation, canvas rendering, navigation, region tabs
- `battle.js` — full dice engine with ALL card abilities, narrator log, ability splashes
- `game.js` — game flow, save/load (localStorage), events, screen management
- `styles.css` — dark spirit-world aesthetic, Creepster + Inter fonts

### Regions (4, unlock by beating bosses)
1. **Frost Valley** (open) — boss: Pelter (7 HP)
2. **Hot Hot Cavern** (beat Pelter) — boss: Stone Cold (9 HP)
3. **Ice Palace** (beat Stone Cold) — boss: King Jay (9 HP)
4. **Dark Castle** (beat King Jay) — boss: The Mountain King (12 HP, final boss)
Region N unlocks when `game.bossesBeaten >= N`. No key items.

### Map Structure
Each region: Start → 2 branches → 3 mid nodes → 2 converge → Boss
Node types: battle, item (chest), event (?), rest (campfire), boss

### Items
- Combat items: Reroll Charm, Spirit Potion (+4 HP), Power Shard (+1 die), Spirit Shield, Lucky Dice
- Boss rewards: Power Shard + Spirit Shield (no keys)

### Battle System (v0.2)
- Complete ability system from Arch — all 36+ abilities implemented
- Narrator log: scrolling color-coded battle story (every roll, ability, damage)
- Ability tags under each card
- Dice animations, glow on matches, triples banner, hit shake
- Ice Shards + Sacred Fires with Winter Barrage/Heating Up modifiers
- Bonus dice support (up to 7)
- Resource bar, items usable mid-battle
- Permadeath — lost ghosts are gone forever

### Built from
~/DrBango/arch/ ("Arch" push) — the Nuzlocke gauntlet mode. Board game wraps the same dice/ability engine in map navigation.

### Starters
Dream Cat, Outlaw, Wim (same as Arch)

### v0.4 changes (2026-04-05) — Real-rules team structure
- **1 active + 2 sideline + reserve inventory** — matches the real game rule from sim-findings. State model: `game.active` (single ghost), `game.sideline[]` (max 2 face-up supporters), `game.reserve[]` (unlimited overflow). Replaces flat `game.collection[]` from v0.3. Save migration in `migrateSave()` handles old saves.
- **Recruitment funnel:** `recruitGhost(ghost)` fills first empty slot (active → sideline → reserve). No cap on recruits; overflow always lands in reserve.
- **Pre-battle:** active fighter fixed; tap a sideline ghost to promote via `promoteSideline(idx)` which swaps active↔sideline in place.
- **Active death:** `handleActiveDeath()` promotes sideline[0] to active, then back-fills sideline from reserve. Game over only when all slots empty. Dead ghosts permadeath.
- **Map HUD:** active slot (larger, accent glow, star marker, "ACTIVE" label), 2 sideline slots (tap to swap), reserve badge showing count (tap opens reserve overlay panel with swap-in buttons).
- **Reserve panel:** modal overlay listing reserve ghosts with ability + HP; "Swap In" button calls `pullFromReserve(i, 0)` which fills empty sideline or swaps with sideline[0].
- **Battle screen:** face-up sideline row rendered under the player card (small portraits + HP) so the 1+2 structure is visible during combat. Passive sideline ability effects NOT yet wired — visual only.
- **Rest nodes:** heal only the active + sideline team (reserve ghosts don't heal at rest).

### Shard/Fire commit mechanic (v0.4)
- **Manual commit before rolling, lost win or lose** — matches real rule from sim-findings.
- State: `committedShards` / `committedFires` (separate from pool `iceShards` / `sacredFires`). Reset to 0 in `startBattle()`.
- UI: during phase 1 (player's turn), pool shards/fires render as dashed "committable" pills with a pulsing outline. Tap to move one from pool → committed. Committed badge is a solid-colored pill; tap to uncommit before rolling.
- Damage application: `resolvePlayerWin` adds `committedShards * (Winter Barrage? 2 : 1)` and `committedFires * (Heating Up? 6 : 3)` to damage, then zeros committed.
- Loss/tie path: `resolveRound` zeros committed before delegating — burnt regardless of outcome.
- `renderResources()` auto-refreshes at phase=1 entry, doPlayerRoll start, and after resolvePlayerWin clears committed.

### v0.5 changes (2026-04-06) — Boss ceremony + key removal
- **Zelda OoT-style boss ceremony:** `showBossCeremony()` in battle.js. Cinematic sequence: screen darkens → light beam descends → relic floats down (cubic-bezier ease) → ring burst on landing → gentle hover with particles. Region-colored (❄️ frost, 🔥 fire, 💎 ice, 👑 crown). Final boss gets grander version (wider beam, bigger relic, 40 particles vs 24). ~5.5s hold.
- **Keys removed entirely:** No more Cavern/Palace/Castle Key items. Regions unlock via `game.bossesBeaten >= regionIndex`. `unlockedAreas` array removed from game state. Key drops removed from `rollItemDrop()`. Resource strip no longer shows keys.
- **Next session:** Map screen cleanup — make it more clean and immersive.

### v0.3 changes (2026-04-05) — Map overhaul + 3-person team
- **3-character team cap:** `MAX_TEAM = 3` in data.js. Start with 1 starter, recruit up to 2 more via events/battle rewards. Permadeath stays — dead ghosts open slots for new recruits. Reward screen shows "Team is full" when at cap.
- **Team HUD:** 3-slot horizontal bar (portrait + name + HP bar). Tap slot to set active ghost. Empty slots are dashed "Empty Slot" placeholders. Separate resource strip below for items/keys/ice/fire.
- **Rest nodes** now heal the **entire party** +3 HP (was just collection[0]).
- **Map visuals:** region banner (name + tagline + boss), atmospheric terrain layer (per-region radial gradients), curved glowing canvas paths, themed node plates with TYPE label + name (`BATTLE · Pelter`, `CHEST · Treasure`, etc.), color-tinted borders per type.
- **Art slot system:** `NODE_ART[type].art` and `REGIONS[i].keyArt` fields are `null` with `[art slot: ...]` dev labels visible on-screen until real images are dropped in. Set those fields to image paths to auto-hide the labels.
- Node layout shifted down slightly (boss y=0.2, start y=0.92) so boss clears the region banner.

name: Spiritkin Art Direction & Midjourney Learnings
description: Comprehensive art direction rules for generating Boo! Battle of Origins Spiritkin concept art via Midjourney, learned through 8+ rounds of iteration
body:
## Art Direction for Spiritkin Concept Art

### What Works (Accepted Generations)
- **"loose watercolor illustration"** as the style anchor — painterly, visible brushstrokes
- **"ethereal creature made of [element]"** as the creature description — Midjourney understands this
- **Creatures IN their environment** — interacting with meadows, swamps, volcanic caves, hot springs
- **Doing something specific** — napping, guarding, peeking, drifting, playing, hatching
- **Unique non-humanoid forms** — shapes you haven't seen before, not based on real animals
- **Charming personality first** — 9/10 cards should be fun/cool/cute for 10-12 year olds
- **Full body visible** — not close-ups, not cropped faces
- **Wispy, ethereal edges** — bodies dissolve, trail, flow into their element

### What Does NOT Work (Rejected Generations)
- **"spiritkin fiend"** — Midjourney doesn't know this term, produces children/random animals
- **Animal anchors** ("fox-like", "raccoon-like", "rabbit-like") — makes generic animals, not unique beings
- **"card game character art style like Pokemon"** — pushes too digital/polished
- **Humanoid figures** — generic human silhouettes, people doing poses
- **Close-ups** — face close-ups lose the character's form
- **White backgrounds with no environment** — characters need their world
- **Too scary/intense** — parents won't buy the game (the Doom lesson from conventions)
- **"loose watercolor sketch"** — "sketch" pushes too pencil-heavy; "illustration" is better
- **Generic action poses** — "slamming fists", "catching a star" defaults to humans doing the action

### The Formula That Works
```
loose watercolor illustration, [size] ethereal creature made of [element] [doing something specific] in [environment], [personality/expression], not a human not a child, a [what kind of being], soft visible brushstrokes
```

### Key Principles
1. **Creature design comes first, action is flavor** — lead with WHAT it is, not WHAT it's doing
2. **Every card is a moment, not a pose** — the creature is caught doing something
3. **The creature IS its element** — not an animal that lives near fire, a being MADE of fire
4. **Wispy + creature = Spiritkin** — the blend of ethereal spirit edges with unique creature forms is the identity
5. **Unpredictable forms** — you shouldn't be able to guess what the next one looks like (like Wim, Stone Cold, Mallow)
6. **1 in 10 can be intense** — most should be charming, one per set gets to be impressive/powerful

name: boobattles-coop-state
description: Boobattles co-op 2v2 mode uses per-player ability state buckets — critical to know before touching coopNextTurn / coopMapToBattle
body:
## The rule

In `~/DrBango/boobattles/`, co-op mode has two players sharing one set of battle-global variables (`pick`, `playerHp`, `playerBonusDice`, `iceShards`, etc.). To keep player-owned ability state from leaking across turn swaps, each player has an ability-state bucket: `coopP1AbilityState`, `coopP2AbilityState` (defined in `orchestrator.js` near `coopMapToBattle`).

**The pattern:** `coopNextTurn` calls `coopSaveActivePlayerAbilityState()` before swapping `coopTurn`, then `coopLoadActivePlayerAbilityState()` after `coopMapToBattle()`. `startCoopBattle` creates both buckets and loads P1's bucket into the globals before the first roll. `coopHandlePlayerDeath` ends by calling `coopNextTurn`, so save/load flows naturally.

## What's in the bucket (per-player)

`bonusDice`, `removeDice`, `iceShards`, `sacredFires`, `bogeyReflectUsed`, `bogeyReflectArmed`, `isFirstRoll`, `playerPrediction`, `round`.

`round` is incremented in `execution.js`'s `nextRound()` co-op branch before calling `coopNextTurn`, so each player's `round` counter advances between their *own* rolls — this is what makes Shade's Haunt (`round > 1`) work.

## What stays shared (enemy-side, intentionally global)

`enemy`, `enemyHp`, `enemyBonusDice`, `enemyRemoveDice`, `enemyIceShards`, `enemySacredFires`, `enemyPrediction`, `enemyHeinousUsed`, `bossScript`, `bossScriptRound`. Only one enemy rolls at a time, and debuffs like Outlaw's Thief set `enemyRemoveDice` on the shared enemy — resetting those on turn swap was the original Thief bug.

## Why this matters

If you add a new ghost ability that touches player-side state, ask: *does this state belong to the ghost that owns the ability, or to whoever is rolling right now?* If the former, add it to the bucket and the save/load helpers. Otherwise you'll silently break it for co-op — the ability will either fire for the wrong player, fire every turn swap, or never fire at all.

Classic failure modes that already happened once: Outlaw's Thief never triggered (removeDice was reset), Bogey reflected every turn (flags were reset), Cave Dweller's Lurk hit every turn (`isFirstRoll` was reset), Shade's Haunt never fired (`round` pinned at 1).

## Also watch

- `enemy.bossHp` is undefined for `coopE2` (the generated partner ghost). Heal caps and rage-HP thresholds must use `enemy.maxHp || enemy.bossHp`. Same goes for `updateHpDisplay` in `presence.js`.
- `startCoopBattle` must apply on-entry abilities (currently just Chad's Sploop!) to *both* player buckets, not just one. Boss entry abilities on `coopE1` still go through the shared `enemyIceShards`.
- `tookDamageLastRound` and `abilityUsedThisBattle` are dead variables — written but never read. Ignore them.

name: feedback_audit-whole-class

body:
When Wyatt reports a bug in one instance of a pattern (one ghost ability, one card, one endpoint, one form field, etc.) and the underlying code has a shared mechanism behind all of them, audit the whole family. Don't ship a one-line fix for just the thing he noticed.

**Why:** Wyatt's exact words after I fixed only Outlaw's Thief: *"I suspect that the thief was in the only ghost not working. To think that it would just be him is a bit naive. Can we look at each ability in the co-op mode and just make sure that each ability will be properly working?"* He correctly assumed the root cause would be a shared-state bug affecting multiple things, and was right — co-op turn-swap was clobbering ability state for at least 7 different ghosts (Outlaw, Bogey, Cave Dweller, Nikon, Shade, Marcus, Kairan, plus Chad's entry effect). He'd rather I spend the time to fix all of them at once than ship one fix, have him find the next bug, repeat.

**How to apply:** When a bug report points at shared infrastructure (turn-based state, damage pipeline, damage-number formatting, API response handler, form validator, etc.), list every consumer of that infrastructure and mentally run each through the broken path. Patch the root cause, not the symptom. If the audit is too big to do in one pass, say so and propose a scope — don't silently only fix the reported case.

The single-symptom fix is the naive move. The family audit is the non-naive move.

name: Simulation Findings — Boo! Spirit Battles
description: Key game balance findings from 23M+ game Monte Carlo simulation, engine bugs identified, and design principles for new cards
body:
## Game Rules (Confirmed)
- Singles=1dmg, Doubles=2dmg, Triples=3dmg. Only winner deals damage. Ties=re-roll.
- Teams: 1 active + 2 reserves (face-up for sideline abilities). Max 1 legendary per team.
- Ice Shards: +1 dmg each, spent before rolling, lost win or lose. Sacred Fires: +3 dmg each, same.
- "Before the roll" is a defined timing window — Masked Hero and Piper counter it.
- "Negated" is a defined game term — Cameron punishes cards that explicitly negate damage (Sky, Patrick, Fang Undercover, Dealer, Kodako).
- All rarities (common through ghost-rare) are balanced equally. Only legendaries are slightly above curve. 1 legendary per team.
- Romy's prediction happens before rolling (before-roll timing).
- Jeffery triggers on ghost KO ("wins a battle" = defeats a ghost), NOT on individual roll wins.
- Doubles tiebreaker: higher UNPAIRED die wins. Triples vs triples: re-roll.

## Key Balance Findings (23M games, pre-bug-fix — directionally correct)
- **HP is king** in a 1-3 damage system. Every HP point = 1-3 extra winning rolls to survive.
- **+1 damage = 33-100% increase.** +2 = 67-200%. These are massive in context.
- **-1 damage (Puff) fires ~44% of the time** (enemy doubles + triples rate). Elite defensive card.
- **Defense/healing dominates the meta.** Shoo appeared in 49/50 top teams as sideline healer.
- **Sideline support is as important as the active fighter** with only 2 slots.
- **Named synergies create deckbuilding identity** (Lou+Grawr, Zach+Guard Thomas, Needle+Buttons).
- **Simple cards can be elite** — Doom (+2 dmg), Puff (-1 dmg), Lucy (+1 on win, 8HP) are top tier through raw math, not complexity.

## Dice Math Reference
- 3 dice: Singles 55.6%, Doubles 41.7%, Triples 2.8%
- 2 dice: Singles 83.3%, Doubles 16.7%, Triples 0% (impossible)
- 3 dice vs 2 dice: 3-dice wins 67%, 2-dice wins 20%, ties 13%
- Kodako's 1-2-3 trigger: 2.78% (6/216). Near-worthless.
- Both players rolling doubles simultaneously: ~17.4%

## Top Cards (directional — sim had Team 2 asymmetry bugs)
- **S-tier:** Hector (singles beat doubles), Piper (-1 die + negate before-roll), Bogey (reflect), Splinter (persistent DOT)
- **A-tier:** Mountain King (9HP + doubles x2), Doom (+2 all wins), Lucy (8HP + +1 wins), Puff (-1 on doubles/triples), Flora (+2HP on doubles), Simon (Sacred Fire on damage taken)
- **Weak:** Kodako (2.78% trigger), Buttons (1HP = instant death, meme card), Toby (AI misplays — needs human judgment)

## Sim Engine Status
- **Location:** /tmp/boo_sim_10k.js (Node.js), /tmp/boo_phase.js (2-phase exhaustive)
- **Known critical bug:** Team 2 ability hooks are incomplete — many abilities (customRoll, afterRoll, onLose, onDefeat, sideline on-win/on-tie) never fire for Team 2. Needs symmetric rewrite before data is trustworthy.
- **Persist flag bug found & partially fixed:** one-time-use flags (_bogeyUsed, _fangUsed, etc.) were resetting every turn. Fixed for both teams but sideline passive flag copying was overwriting persist flags — fixed by filtering persistKeys.
- **NOT production-ready.** Useful for directional findings but full rewrite needed for definitive rankings.

## Design Principles for New Cards (86 needed to reach 200)
1. Every card must work as BOTH a fighter AND a potential reserve — no pure sideline-only dead weight
2. HP matters enormously — don't give away HP cheaply
3. New cards should answer the defense/healing meta, not just add more defense
4. Named synergies and before-roll interactions create interesting deckbuilding
5. Simple mechanics can be elite — complexity isn't required for power
6. Trigger probability matters — abilities that fire <5% of the time feel like no ability at all (Kodako)
7. Cards need clear timing keywords (before rolling, when, upon, while, if)

## Player Archetypes (for future sim AI)
- **Risk Taker:** leads glass cannons, spends resources immediately, goes all-in
- **Funky Combo Guy:** orders team for synergy setups, holds resources for payoff turns
- **Simple Man:** highest HP leads, spends resources when available, no tricks

**Why:** Wyatt wants sim AI to play cards practically based on real player personality types, not just optimal math.

**Ghosts (4 — 3 starters + 1 unlockable):**
- The Mountain King — 9 HP, "Beast Mode" (doubles deal 2X damage), fiery orange theme, tagline: "Doubles hit twice as hard."
- Lucy — 8 HP, "Blue Fire" (win a roll → +1 bonus damage), icy blue theme, tagline: "Every victory burns hot!"
- Prince Balatron — 6 HP, "Party Time" (lose a roll & survive → player taps to roll 1 counter die), gold name / purple tagline, tagline: "Lose a roll? The party's just getting started."
- **Romy** (UNLOCKABLE) — 8 HP, "Valley Guardian" (predict a number 1-6 before rolling, if any die matches → +3 damage), frost blue theme, tagline: "Trust your instincts."

**Card image sources:** ~/DrBango/boo/cards/ — lucy.png, mountain_king.png, balatron.png, romy.png
**Unused card art in cards/:** doom.png, shade.png (removed from roster but files remain)

**Unlock system:**
- Game 1: Only original 3 (MK, Lucy, Balatron)
- First replay (gamesPlayed === 1): Romy guaranteed in center slot + 2 random originals, NEW badge shown
- All replays after: Random 3 from full pool of 4
- Tracks gamesPlayed, wins, losses in localStorage (keys: boo_gamesPlayed, boo_wins, boo_losses)
- Tracks per-ghost wins in localStorage (key: boo_ghostWins — JSON object keyed by cssClass)
- W/L record shown on pick screen after first game ("3W — 1L")
- Crown badge (👑) shown on pick cards for ghosts you've already won with

**Flow:**
1. **Pick screen** — Deep ocean blue background with floating spirit orbs + sweeping light rays. Rules at top ("Roll the most matching dice!"), "Choose your ghost / Pick which one speaks to you..", 3 cards side by side, selecting one shows themed name + tagline, then Fight button. W/L record below Fight button after first game.
2. **"Start" overlay** — Big centered cyan text punches in before battle begins, dice area hidden until it fades
3. **Battle screen** — Pokemon-style layout: enemy top-right with name plate + HP bar, player bottom-left with name plate + HP bar, dice centered vertically, narrator + roll button below. First enemy roll shakes slightly longer (1.1s vs 0.7s) so player can orient. For Romy: 6-button prediction picker replaces roll button each round.
4. **Multi-round combat** — Real dice rolls with player boosts, abilities trigger with dramatic splashes + ghost card pops to foreground above dark overlay
5. **Crash animation** on win — player card charges into enemy, impact flash + screen shake, enemy shatters into 20 physics shards
6. **CTA screen** — "You Win!" or "You Lose!", ghost card, "200 unique ghosts" pitch, Kickstarter button → BattleOfOrigins.com, Play Again

**Ability splash themes (full-screen overlays with glow + SFX):**
- Beast Mode: fiery orange/red radial gradient
- Blue Fire: icy blue radial gradient
- Party Time: purple/pink radial gradient + counter die tap UI
- Valley Guardian: frost blue aurora gradient, shows "Valley Guardian" title + "Prediction Nailed! +3 Damage!" subtitle

**Hidden player boost system (organic games only):**
- Base: 6% triples chance, 5% double-6s chance
- Desperate (HP ≤ 2): +8% to both
- Counter enemy triples: +6% more triples chance
- Counter enemy high doubles (4-6): 20% chance to auto-beat with doubles one higher
- Enemy near death (HP ≤ 1): boosts reduced (3% triples, 2% doubles) so kill shot feels earned
- Romy prediction nudge: 40% chance one die lands on predicted number

**Scripted Scenarios (70% chance for Hercules/Pluto/Oracle, 30% for Atlas):**
Each ghost has a cinematic scenario with dice variance ±2 each play (shift rejects any value that would change roll type due to clamping):
- **Hercules** (Lucy vs Mountain King) — Desperation → hope → euphoria. Beaten to 2 HP by Beast Mode, comeback with doubles, climax = player triples beating enemy triples. 6 rounds.
- **Atlas** (Mountain King vs Lucy) — Last stand. Beaten to 1 HP by Blue Fire over 3 rounds, barely survives with singles, Beast Mode doubles 5s swing, triple 4s finisher. 6 rounds.
- **Pluto** (Balatron vs Lucy) — Knife fight anxiety. Trading blows, both near death, player LOSES final roll but Party Time counter die kills enemy with exactly enough damage. 3 rounds.
- **Oracle** (Romy vs Mountain King) — Prediction clutch. Beast Mode opener smashes to 4/8, then prediction-powered singles and doubles finish MK. Player always picks their own prediction (no auto-pick). 3 rounds.

**Music & SFX:**
- BGG.mp3 — background music, starts on Fight, loops, fades out on win/loss. Hard-stopped on replay to prevent crash.
- DiceRoll.mp3 — plays when player clicks Roll
- 1Damage/2Damage/3Damage.mp3 — based on damage dealt
- triples.mp3 — loud SFX on any triples roll
- Special.mp3 — plays when any ability activates
- Shatter.mp3 — crash animation

**Visual effects:**
- Triples: mega-glow dice, screen flash, screen shake, huge "TRIPLES!" banner in roller's color
- Ability splashes: full-screen themed overlay + ghost card floats to foreground (z-index 950, scale 1.10, brightness 1.2) then returns after
- HP bars: thick gradient fills with glass shine, glow, yellow at 50%, red + pulse at 25%
- Hit animations: card shake on damage
- Crash: card-slam → white flash → 20-shard shatter → winner glow → sparkle bursts
- Pick screen: ocean blue gradient + floating warm/cool orbs + sweeping light rays
- Ghost select: themed name + tagline with colored glow, other cards dim
- Snow particles on CTA screen

**Design decisions:**
- Only 3 ghost choices per screen — simpler, faster, more intentional
- 1v1 not 3v3 — reduces complexity for first-time viewer
- No game jargon — narrator uses plain English
- Portrait-optimized for mobile/embed
- Mountain King always first (left position) in pick grid on first game
- Romy unlocks after first game to reward replay and showcase different mechanics
- Doom and Shade designed but pulled from roster (art remains in cards/ for future use)

## Name
**BOO: Battle of Origins** — "BOO" is an acronym for the in-world ritual tournament

## Core Concepts
- **Spiritkin:** Living manifestations of power drawn from the essence of their origin regions
- **The BOO:** A ritual tournament where disputes between regions are settled — not through destruction, but outmaneuvering
- **Wills:** Fragments of light released when corrupted Spiritkin are restored; absorbed by the lantern
- **The Lantern:** Grandfather's artifact, blue flame, houses Spiritkin companions, grows brighter as Toby progresses
- **The Overworld:** The spirit realm containing all regions (Rolling Hills, Frost Valley, Dark Castle, Dark Valley, etc.)

## Story
- **Toby:** Human boy, visits grandfather's house when parents travel
- **Grandfather:** Former Spiritkin Grand Master, disappeared after a rigged final match — trapped by Valkin the Grand
- **Spark:** Toby's first Spiritkin companion, a dog spirit summoned via a tennis ball
- **Valkin the Grand:** Antagonist, seeks to control the BOO itself to reshape the world — rejects balance, wants control
- **Toby's quest:** Free corrupted Spiritkin, power up the lantern, find his grandfather

## Video Game Concept (separate from card game)
- Lantern evolves: starts carrying 1 Spiritkin, eventually 3
- Spiritkin grant elemental powers (fire, ice, lightning) for puzzle-solving
- Knob on lantern switches active Spiritkin
- Combat: hero Spiritkin + 2 sideline echoes
- Items tether freed Spiritkin as echoes; backpack has limited capacity
- Willpower as health resource — if Toby hits 0, lantern goes out = game over
- Must return to grandfather's house to swap team

## Terminology Question
- Lore says "Spiritkin," existing cards say "ghosts" — needs resolution

- Not yet finalized or shared with Brim Studio

name: Work Principles from Power-User Reference
description: Key working principles Wyatt endorsed — verification, autonomous fixes, re-planning, elegance balance
body:
**Verification Before Done:** Never call a task complete without proving it works. Run tests, check logs, diff behavior. Gut-check: "Would a staff engineer approve this?"
**Why:** Prevents shipping broken code and reduces back-and-forth.
**How to apply:** Before presenting any code change as done, verify it actually works.

**Autonomous Bug Fixing:** When given a bug report, just fix it. Don't ask for hand-holding. Point at logs/errors/failing tests, then resolve them.
**Why:** Wyatt moves fast and doesn't want to context-switch to guide debugging.
**How to apply:** When a bug is reported or a test fails, diagnose and fix it proactively instead of asking clarifying questions.

**Stop and Re-plan When Sideways:** If something goes sideways during implementation, STOP and re-plan immediately — don't keep pushing a broken approach.
**Why:** Brute-forcing a bad path wastes time and creates messy code.
**How to apply:** If an approach hits 2+ unexpected blockers, pause and reassess instead of hacking around them.

**Elegance — Balanced:** For non-trivial changes, pause and ask "is there a more elegant way?" But skip this for simple, obvious fixes — don't over-engineer.
**Why:** Working code > clever code for a shipping product, but avoid accumulating tech debt on bigger changes.
**How to apply:** Only demand elegance on structural/architectural changes. Quick fixes should stay quick.

name: feedback_cmyk-conversion
description: When converting print-ready CMYK PDFs to web images, must use ICC color profiles to avoid washed-out colors
body:
When extracting images from Boo! Spirit Battles print-ready PDFs (CMYK color space), do NOT use basic `-colorspace sRGB`. This produces washed-out, desaturated colors.

**Why:** The card PDFs from Bayaya are CMYK print files. A raw colorspace swap doesn't properly map color channels, resulting in noticeable color distortion (especially reds, oranges, purples).

**How to apply:** Always use ICC profile conversion:
```
magick -density 300 input.pdf \
  -profile "/System/Library/ColorSync/Profiles/Generic CMYK Profile.icc" \
  -profile "/System/Library/ColorSync/Profiles/sRGB Profile.icc" \
  -resize x600 -quality 92 output.jpg
```

name: Holotexture Design Workflow
description: How to create holographic texture overlays for Boo! Spirit Battles cards — tools, techniques, lessons learned
body:
Holotexture files are black/white PNGs (825x1125) where white = holo, black = non-holo. Used for Frost Valley Purple Ghost Rare cards.

**Key lessons:**
- For symbols (hearts, spades, etc): render from **Arial Unicode font glyphs** (`/Library/Fonts/Arial Unicode.ttf`) — they look way better than hand-drawn geometry
- Always place **largest elements first** (snowflakes) with collision tracking, then smaller ones (hearts/spades) check against them
- Snowflake collision radius must include **arm reach + ~20px buffer**, not just center size
- Tracing card art magic with bezier curves is very hard to get pixel-perfect — if close isn't good enough, a simple minimal texture (snow dots, symbols) can be a better compromise
- Pixel-based color extraction (HSV thresholds) doesn't work well when magic and background share similar blue hues
- `poppler` needed for PDF reading on Mac (`brew install poppler`)

**Cards with holotextures created:**
- **Eloise** — hearts + snowflakes + snow dots (Change of Heart theme)
- **Gary** — winter breeze snow dots + tiny snowflakes + sparkles (minimal)
- **Spades card** — font-rendered ♠ spades + snowflakes + snow dots

**Why:** Holotextures are needed for the manufacturer (Bayaya) for the Frost Valley reprint batch.
**How to apply:** When creating new holotextures, start minimal (symbols + snow) and add complexity only if requested. Use font glyphs for card suit symbols.

name: Chrome Browser Automation
description: How to control Chrome from Claude Code using AppleScript, JavaScript injection, cliclick, and screencapture for GUI automation tasks
body:
## Prerequisites
- **Chrome setting required:** View → Developer → Allow JavaScript from Apple Events (must be enabled once)
- **Tools installed:** `cliclick` (via homebrew), `pyautogui` (pip), `discord.py` (pip)

## Core Techniques

### 1. Open Chrome to a URL
```bash
open -a "Google Chrome" "https://example.com"
# Or navigate existing tab:
osascript -e 'tell application "Google Chrome" to set URL of active tab of front window to "https://example.com"'
```

### 2. Read page content via JavaScript
```bash
osascript <<'EOF'
tell application "Google Chrome"
    tell active tab of front window
        set r to execute javascript "document.body.innerText.substring(0, 1000)"
        return r
    end tell
end tell
EOF
```

### 3. Click elements via JavaScript
```bash
osascript <<'EOF'
tell application "Google Chrome"
    tell active tab of front window
        execute javascript "var buttons = document.querySelectorAll('button'); for (var i = 0; i < buttons.length; i++) { if (buttons[i].textContent.trim() === 'Submit') { buttons[i].click(); break; } }"
    end tell
end tell
EOF
```

### 4. Get element coordinates (for physical clicks)
```bash
# Get viewport offset: Chrome window screenY + (outerHeight - innerHeight) = viewport top
osascript <<'EOF'
tell application "Google Chrome"
    tell active tab of front window
        execute javascript "'' + window.screenX + ',' + window.screenY + ',' + window.outerHeight + ',' + window.innerHeight"
    end tell
end tell
EOF
# viewport_top_y = screenY + (outerHeight - innerHeight)
# screen_coords: x = screenX + js_x, y = viewport_top_y + js_y
```

### 5. Physical clicks with cliclick (for React/custom components that ignore JS .click())
```bash
cliclick c:720,500       # click at screen coordinates
cliclick t:"some text"   # type text
```

### 6. Keyboard input for React inputs (when programmatic value setting doesn't work)
```bash
osascript <<'EOF'
tell application "Google Chrome"
    activate
    tell active tab of front window
        execute javascript "document.querySelector('input').focus()"
    end tell
end tell
tell application "System Events"
    keystroke "text to type"
end tell
EOF
```

### 7. Read clipboard after clicking Copy buttons
```bash
cliclick c:<copy_button_x>,<copy_button_y>
sleep 1
pbpaste
```

### 8. Screenshots (NOTE: Screen Recording permission needed for Terminal to capture Chrome content)
```bash
screencapture -x /tmp/screen.png
```

## Key Gotchas
- **Retina displays:** `window.devicePixelRatio` = 2, but cliclick uses screen points (same as CSS pixels on Mac)
- **React inputs:** `input.value = "x"` doesn't trigger React state. Use keyboard simulation instead.
- **AppleScript JS returns:** Complex objects return `missing value`. Use simple string concatenation, not JSON.stringify.
- **Modal/overlay blocking:** Discord's "App Launched" overlay blocks auth forms. Remove with `element.style.display = 'none'`.
- **2FA:** Cannot be bypassed programmatically — requires user's authenticator app.
